annotations.title: Where a published statement comes from

description: Use this before you quote, cite or hand on anything from this graph, and whenever a reader asks on what authority a statement rests. It returns, for one object, every statement with its kind, its primary source, the locator inside that source and the review metadata, plus the source records behind those citations and a ready made citation block with the identifier, the object version, the payload hash and the release. Works for any object type, not only obligations. Take the identifier from earlier tool output; a short form such as art. 26 resolves when it points at one obligation, else error_code and suggestions come back.

detail.description: Amount of data to return. brief keeps the outcome, the dates, the reasons, the open questions and the source with its locator; full adds the complete objects, every statement text and every hash, for re-computation or archiving.

entity_id.description: The stable identifier of any object, for example praxikon:eu:ai-act:guidance:... or praxikon:eu:ai-act:obligation:... . An identifier in the flat raip:<type>:<slug> form published up to dataset 1.1.0 resolves to the same object.

lang.description: Language of the labels and explanations. Dutch is the default.

name: get_source_provenance

pin.description: The release and the two time axes this answer resolved against. Store it next to anything you keep: an unpinned query is not reproducible, because the defaults move with each release.

provenance.description: Which published endpoints produced this result. Every call is listed with its full URL, so a reader can re-issue it and check the answer rather than trust it.

items.description: A record in the register of primary documents. source_record_hash_sha256 covers only the three fields named in fingerprint_basis: it attests that we checked this document, in this edition, on this date. It is not a content hash of the external page and not an archive copy.

One statement inside an object. kind is load bearing: official_fact is attributable to a named primary source and is source checked, editorial_interpretation and recommended_action are Praxikon work. Do not merge the three.

title: Where a published statement comes from
